The kit steals passwords, crypto wallets and Discord accounts, and it also mines Monero in the background. Seqrite Labs found a newer build of the kit on an infected Windows machine and rebuilt its full logic. ArmorSteal malware ArmorSteal reaches victims through search results.

findings.summary: SonicWall has fixed an exploited SonicOS SSL-VPN vulnerability (CVE-2026-19868) that may allow attackers with valid credentials to bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication. With no workarounds listed, the company has urged admins to patch quickly. About CVE-2026-19868 CVE-2026-19868 is an authentication enforcement flaw in the SonicOS SSL-VPN service, and is exploitable only if SAML is enabled for SSL-VPN logins.
findings.title: Exploited SonicWall SSL-VPN flaw lets attackers bypass SAML-enforced MFA (CVE-2026-19868)

findings.summary: Two high-severity flaws have been disclosed in ModSecurity, the open-source web application firewall (WAF) used with Apache, IIS, and Nginx. Two GitHub advisories published by maintainer airween on September 30 describe flaws allowing malicious file uploads and server crashes that could lead to remote code execution. ModSecurity inspects web traffic and blocks requests that look harmful. Many sites depend on it, so any gap in how it reads a request matters.

On November 5, five US agencies warned of ongoing attacks on refrigeration and cold chain systems.

findings.summary: ### Summary fastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits an operation's `summary` as the generated route handler's docstring, using a triple-quoted string without escaping `"""`. A `"""` in the summary closes the docstring and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that becomes an expression statement in the handler body -- which runs when the route handler is CALLED (the endpoint is hit). The summary is a pure data field. Verified on fastapi-code-generator 0.8.0 / Python 3 / FastAPI.
findings.title: fastapi-code-generator: Call-time RCE via operation summary -> unescaped route-handler docstring

findings.summary: ### Summary `ZipUtil.unpack(...)` rejects ZIP entries that escape the target output directory, but the `Zips` fluent API appears to use a separate unpack implementation that does not apply the same destination-boundary check. A ZIP entry such as: ```text ../escape/poc.txt ``` is written outside the configured destination directory when processed with: ```java Zips.get(zip).unpack().destination(outputDir).process(); ``` The transformer branch is affected as well.
findings.title: zt-zip: Path traversal in fluent API unpack

findings.summary: ### Summary fastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits the OpenAPI path into the generated main.py route decorator as a single-quoted string literal (`@app.get('/u/ /x')`) without escaping the `'`. A `'` in the path closes the decorator string and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that the decorator argument evaluates when main.py is imported (the ASGI server imports it at startup) -- code execution, no request needed. The path is a pure data field.
findings.title: fastapi-code-generator: Import-time RCE via route path -> unescaped @app.get('...') decorator

findings.summary: ### Summary fastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits an operation's extra responses into the route decorator's responses={...} dict, using each response's status-code key as a single-quoted string literal without escaping the '. A ' in a status-code key closes the dict-key string and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that the decorator argument evaluates when main.py is imported (the ASGI server imports it at startup) -- code execution, no request.
findings.title: fastapi-code-generator: Import-time RCE via response status-code key -> unescaped @app.get(..., responses={...}) dict

findings.summary: ### Summary Path traversal in the Signal K resources and applicationData APIs lets an unauthenticated or low-privileged user read, write and delete files outside the storage root. Reading /security.json discloses the JWT signing secret, enabling admin token forgery and remote code execution. ### Details ## Description The v2 REST resources API `GET /signalk/v2/api/resources/:resourceType/:resourceId` passes `resourceId` to `FileStore.getResource()` without validation.
findings.title: Signal K resources API path traversal can disclose the JWT signing secret and enable remote code execution

findings.summary: In OAuth2 silent authorization (`prompt=none`), when the `scope` parameter was empty or omitted, all scopes registered for the OAuth client became eligible for issuance. However, the prior consent check was performed against the empty requested scope set. As a result, an attacker could obtain an access token with broader scopes than the user had previously consented to, without requiring additional consent.
findings.title: traQ: Privilege escalation by OAuth prompt=none request

findings.summary: ### Impact For instances where `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE` is set to `local`, the file retrieval API `/files/{fileId}` could serve user-uploaded SVG or HTML files in a way that allowed them to be rendered directly in the browser. As a result, an attacker who can upload files to traQ could upload a crafted SVG or HTML file and trick a victim into opening the file URL, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. ### Patches This issue has been fixed in v3.28.3.
findings.title: traQ: XSS in the User Uploaded File Retrieval API

findings.summary: ### Summary The HTTP server mode of `@tsparticles/mcp-server` accumulates all incoming request body chunks into an in-memory `Buffer[]` array with no size limit before calling `JSON.parse`. An unauthenticated remote attacker can stream an arbitrarily large body to `POST /mcp`, exhausting the Node.js process memory and causing a Denial of Service.
findings.title: tsParticles: Unbounded HTTP Request Body Buffering in @tsparticles/mcp-server Leads to Remote DoS

findings.summary: ### Summary The `readPsd()` function in `ag-psd` accepts a `totalMemoryLimit` option to cap memory usage when parsing untrusted PSD files, but this limit is never forwarded to the layer image buffer allocation path. A property name mismatch (`totalMemoryLimit` vs. `memoryLimit`) causes the size guard inside `createImageDataBitDepth` to be skipped unconditionally.
findings.title: ag-psd: Uncontrolled Memory Allocation in PSD Layer Decoding (totalMemoryLimit bypass)

Version `4.3.1` appears to fix this by returning HTTP 400 for invalid JSON.

findings.summary: ## Summary The client credentials grant (`grant_type=client_credentials`) does not validate the resource parameter before embedding it as the aud claim in the issued JWT. Any authenticated OIDC client can obtain a Pocket ID-signed access token claiming authorization for any arbitrary audience, including other registered OIDC clients. There is no check that the requested audience is a registered resource server, and no check that the requesting client has been granted permission to access it.

findings.summary: ## Summary Telepresence's Traffic Manager gRPC API (port 8081) requires no authentication. Any pod with cluster-network access to the Traffic Manager can register as a client in an arbitrary managed namespace and create intercepts against services in that namespace, regardless of Kubernetes RBAC. On interception the victim pod's complete container environment (secrets, tokens, API keys) is delivered to the attacker. Tested on HEAD v2.28.0, commit b2231a4.
findings.title: Telepresence: Traffic Manager gRPC has no auth — any pod claims arbitrary namespace and intercepts services, receiving victim environment secrets

findings.summary: ## Summary The Traffic Manager `Tunnel` gRPC streaming endpoint accepts a session ID from the first bytes of the client-controlled message payload. No verification confirms the caller owns the session. An attacker supplying a valid active session ID receives a fully routed tunnel for that session, gaining the network routing capabilities of the legitimate Telepresence client. Tested on HEAD v2.28.0, commit b2231a4.
findings.title: Telepresence: Tunnel endpoint accepts caller-supplied session ID with no ownership proof — active client sessions hijackable

findings.summary: ### Summary zizmor 1.27.0 exposes GitHub access tokens in cleartext when debug-level logging is enabled. Tokens supplied via environment variables (`GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN`), or the corresponding command-line options (`--gh-token`, `--github-token`, `--zizmor-github-token`) are included in the debug representation of the parsed application configuration and written to stderr.
findings.title: zizmor: Debug logging prints available GitHub credentials in cleartext

findings.summary: ### Summary The documented `web.NewHandler` static file server can read files outside `Config.AppDir` when the request path contains URL-encoded dot-segments such as `%2e%2e`. Go's `ServeMux` redirects plain `/../` paths, but it passes encoded dot-segments to the handler after decoding `r.URL.Path`.
findings.title: esm.sh: web.NewHandler allows arbitrary file read via encoded dot-segment path traversal

findings.summary: ### Impact In GPUStack before v2.2.0, `get_current_user` (in `gpustack/api/auth.py`) promotes any request whose source is considered loopback to the built-in administrator account when `force_auth_localhost` is `False` (the default). The "source" is derived by `client_ip_getter`, which can be made to report `127.0.0.1` without any credentials in two ways: 1.
findings.title: GPUStack: Authentication bypass via trusted loopback source (reverse-proxy TCP peer or X-GPUStack-Real-IP header) grants unauthenticated admin

findings.summary: ## Summary An authenticated Pocket ID user can request an email-verification token while their account uses an address they control, change the account email address, and then redeem the previously issued token. The token is bound only to the user ID, not to the address to which it was sent, and changing the address does not revoke outstanding tokens. As a result, Pocket ID marks the newly supplied address as verified even though the user never proved control of it.

findings.summary: ### Summary The TCP transporter's packet parser (`src/transporters/tcp/parser.js`) reads the packet length field with `Buffer.prototype.readInt32BE`, a signed read. A crafted packet whose length field has the sign bit set yields a negative `length`. The parser then advances past the parsed message with `packet = packet.slice(length)`, but `Buffer.prototype.slice` clamps an out-of-range negative start index to `0`, so the buffer is returned unchanged.
findings.title: Moleculer: Unauthenticated Denial of Service via negative length field in the TCP transporter packet parser

findings.summary: Russia-aligned group Turla planted a modular .NET toolset on Microsoft Exchange servers at two government organizations, one in Kazakhstan and one in Romania, and used it to copy selected email straight out of the mail flow. ESET researchers found the malware and named it Cereal. The toolset doesn’t need an attacker-owned server. Operators send commands to the victim’s internet-facing Exchange server, dressed up as ordinary Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover, and ActiveSync traffic.

findings.summary: ### Summary `fastMerkleRoot` pads an odd level by hashing the last node with itself. It does not report that it did so, and `checkTxRoots` never looks for repeated transactions. A peer can therefore duplicate transactions to fill the pad and produce a block with a different transaction list but the same merkle root. The block hash and block id do not change, so the header still carries valid proof of work.
findings.title: bitcoinjs-lib: Undetected merkle node duplication in block root computation validates a forged transaction list

findings.summary: ### Impact The callback Base64-decodes the posted XML, reads NameID and attributes, resolves or provisions the user, and mints a gpustack_session JWT — but never calls OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response(), the step that verifies the signature, issuer, audience, destination, and time conditions. No credentials are required, and SAML SSO does not even need to be configured.
findings.title: GPUStack: SAML callback trusts an unverified SAMLResponse, allowing authentication bypass and account takeover

This follows the inheritance model defined by OPC UA Part 3, §5.2.9, where nodes without an explicit `RolePermissions` attribute inherit the namespace `DefaultRolePermissions`.

A common cause of this vulnerability is the failure to validate user-supplied data before displaying it within the vulnerable application without proper filtering.
findings.title: OHIF Viewers: DOM-Based Cross Site Scripting (XSS) through MIME type of document

findings.summary: ### Summary `asn1.fromDer()` decodes the contents of BIT STRINGs as ASN.1 by default. That decode ignored the `maxDepth` recursion limit (an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66031) and also decoded nested BIT STRINGs, keeping a full copy of the decoded contents at each level, so small crafted DER or PEM inputs (certificates, keys, PKCS structures) use excessive CPU time and memory and can abort the Node.js process. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.
findings.title: Forge: ASN.1 resource exhaustion via BIT STRING decoding in asn1.fromDer

Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.
findings.title: Forge: ASN.1 resource exhaustion via BIT STRING decoding in asn1.fromDer

findings.summary: ### Summary RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signature verification (`publicKey.verify()` with the default scheme, also used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 verification) accepted non-canonical BER encodings of the DigestInfo, such as NULL parameters with content and non-minimal lengths. These leave attacker-controlled bytes inside an accepted DigestInfo, which allows signatures to be forged without the private key for RSA keys with a low public exponent (e=3). Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1.
findings.title: Forge: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery via non-canonical DigestInfo encoding

findings.summary: ### Impact An authenticated non-administrative user could access a Kubernetes cluster they are not authorized to access through GPUStack's Kubernetes API proxy. The `cluster_apiserver_proxy` handler did not perform a resource-level authorization check before forwarding requests to the selected cluster. Requests were forwarded through a worker using its Kubernetes ServiceAccount credentials.
findings.title: GPUStack: Missing authorization on several cluster and resource endpoints allows cross-user access and cluster takeover

findings.title: AG2: Newline injection in SandboxShellTool bypasses allowed=[...] and readonly=True, enabling arbitrary command execution

findings.summary: ### Summary The `POST /__nuxt_content/:collection/query` endpoint in `@nuxt/content` accepts an attacker-controlled `sql` field from the HTTP request body and executes it against a local SQLite database after passing it through an insufficient validator (`assertSafeQuery`). The validator only blocks a small set of SQL command keywords and does not reject expensive SQLite built-in functions such as `randomblob()`, `zeroblob()`, `hex()`, or `length()`.
findings.title: Nuxt Content: Unauthenticated SQLite Function DoS via Content Query API

Two critical vulnerabilities in Endpoint Manager and CSA present the highest risks. Ivanti said it was not aware of customers being exploited through these vulnerabilities before public disclosure.
findings.title: Ivanti Patches New Security Flaws Affecting Endpoint Manager, EPMM, Sentry, CSA, and Workspace Manager

findings.summary: SAP has released fixes for PROXYGATE and ICM2SHELL, critical security flaws that could let attackers take control of SAP systems without signing in. Disclosed during the November 10, 2026, Security Patch Day , the vulnerabilities carry maximum CVSS scores of 10.0 and affect core components used across business applications. Onapsis Research Labs discovered and reported both issues.

findings.summary: The BYOD ransomware group has allegedly claimed a Toyota data breach, saying it obtained personal information and access involving kiosk devices. A supplied screenshot shows a Toyota listing updated on November 10, 2026. The claim remains unverified, and the material does not establish that Toyota’s systems were breached or that files were encrypted. The listing names full names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth among the allegedly exposed information.

findings.summary: Microsoft Office Outlook contains a missing user interaction for potentially unsafe action vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.
findings.title: Microsoft Office Outlook Missing User Interaction for Potentially Unsafe Action Vulnerability

findings.summary: Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder contains an incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability that may allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the Webmail experience.
findings.title: Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres Vulnerability

findings.summary: Cisco BroadWorks contains an improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system.
findings.title: Cisco BroadWorks Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference Vulnerability

findings.summary: Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG), Load Balancer, Application Delivery Controller (ADC), Message Archiver (BMA), WAF Control Center (WCC), Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Web Security Gateway (WSG) contain an OS command injection vulnerability. This vulnerability could allow an authenticated administrator to inject OS commands that execute with root privileges when the crafted timezone value is subsequently processed. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-116606
findings.title: Barracuda Networks Multiple Products OS Command Injection Vulnerability

findings.summary: Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted, compatible backup archive, resulting in unauthorized modification of the appliance’s global configuration. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-111560.
findings.title: Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability

findings.summary: Google Chromium contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XML component that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a specially crafted webpage. This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera.
findings.title: Google Chromium Use-After-Free Vulnerability

One of the vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing vulnerability in Outlook, is already being exploited. Other vulnerabilities of note: CVE-2026-119958: A critical RCE vulnerability in Microsoft LDAP.

findings.summary: ## Summary `Rack::Multipart::Parser` reads the request body in chunks of `rack.multipart.buffer_size` (1 MiB by default) into an internal scan buffer. Parsed bytes are only discarded from that buffer when a chunk ends inside a part body. A request whose parts are sized so that every chunk ends inside, or immediately after, a part's headers is never compacted, so the buffer grows to the size of the request.
findings.title: Rack: Multipart parsing allows DoS via unbounded scan buffer growth

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. SignalR Redis scale-out can mishandle case-mismatched group removal and leave subscriptions in a state that permits persistent resource amplification and denial of service.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114147 - ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. SignalR connections are not consistently bound to the identity negotiated at connection establishment, allowing injected messages to execute Hub invocations as the victim.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114146 - ASP.NET Core Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. An insecure temporary directory used by Aspire CLI-generated builds can allow a local attacker to influence MSBuild response-file discovery and execute code with the privileges of the developer running the CLI.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120778 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. A crafted PDB `LF_DECIMAL` payload can trigger an out-of-bounds stack write when processed by DIA.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114151 - Visual Studio Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. A Portable PDB `EmbeddedSource` record with parent RID 0 can trigger an out-of-bounds write.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114158 - Visual Studio Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. An oversized Portable PDB document name can be truncated during allocation and cause a heap out-of-bounds write.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114159 - Visual Studio Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Insecure temporary files used by Aspire CLI can allow a local attacker to obtain sensitive configuration information.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120792 - Aspire Information Disclosure Vulnerability

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Crafted PDB line metadata can exceed the caller-provided buffer and cause a heap out-of-bounds write.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118745 - Visual Studio Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Attacker-controlled COFF relocation offsets can cause an out-of-bounds stack write in `DiaObjectFile::ApplyFixup`.
findings.title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114152 - Visual Studio Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

findings.summary: Microsoft has released its monthly security update for November 2026, which includes 1095 vulnerabilities affecting a range of products, including 64 that Microsoft marked as "critical." Microsoft notes that 1 of the vulnerabilities disclosed this month have been exploited in the wild CVE-2026-124194 affects Microsoft Office Outlook. CVE-2026-124194 is a spoofing vulnerability involving Product UI does not Warn User of Unsafe Actions and has a CVSS base score of 6.5.

CVE-2026-124194 is a spoofing vulnerability involving Product UI does not Warn User of Unsafe Actions and has a CVSS base score of 6.5.

findings.summary: Microsoft has confirmed that hackers are exploiting an Outlook zero-day that can expose Windows authentication information when a user opens a malicious file. Tracked as CVE-2026-124194, the spoofing vulnerability was patched on November 10, 2026. Microsoft marks it “Exploitation Detected” and says it was not publicly disclosed before the update. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 6.5 and a Moderate severity rating. However, confirmed attacks make it a patching priority.
findings.title: Microsoft Confirms Hackers Are Exploiting Outlook 0-Day to Steal Windows Authentication Hashes

findings.summary: Fortinet has disclosed critical security flaws affecting FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, and FortiOS, including weaknesses that could let attackers execute code without logging in. Published on November 10, 2026, the disclosures cover management APIs, device communication services, routing, and specific high availability setups. Attack requirements differ, making enabled features and network access central to assessing exposure.
findings.title: Critical Fortinet Flaws Expose FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer to Remote Code Execution Without Login

findings.summary: A new hacking toolkit called GhostFrame gives criminals a single control panel for taking over VMware ESXi servers and the virtual machines that run on them. Researchers at Recorded Future’s Insikt Group found the framework while tracking a group named TAG-218, whose activity overlaps with Settra ransomware. The tool can also pull Windows passwords out of hosted machines without ever running a program inside them. The key point is where GhostFrame works.
findings.title: New GhostFrame Malware Lets Hackers Hijack VMware ESXi VMs and Steal Windows Credentials

findings.summary: Research has tied three seemingly unrelated espionage campaigns to a single supplier of Chinese-nexus tooling, which it tracks as CopperDragon. It may act as a “digital quartermaster,” supplying tools to several China-nexus actors, including FamousSparrow, Earth Estries, TropicTrooper and UAT-9244. The clusters, named SilentDelivery, OceanGate and DarkWire, hit telecommunications providers, government bodies, military entities, research […]

findings.summary: In recent years, cyberthreats have increasingly taken a hybrid approach, combining time-tested techniques for advancing through infrastructure, modern methods of evading network filters, and automation powered by large language models. This is also the approach of Citrus Ransomware, a previously undocumented group whose toolset includes VLESS tunnels (used to disguise traffic as regular HTTPS) and a ransomware Trojan from the Sn00py family.

findings.summary: ClickFix attacks are moving beyond simple malware downloads, with recent investigations revealing executable payloads hidden inside PNG images and intrusions reaching Windows domain controllers. The activity shows how a fake verification prompt can become the starting point for persistent access, credential theft, and movement across corporate networks. The trick still depends on convincing someone to run a command copied from a webpage.
findings.title: ClickFix Attacks Evolve to Hide Malware in PNG Images and Hijack Windows Domain Controllers

The total falls below October’s Patch Tuesday (1,413 flaws) but still makes this the second-largest monthly release on record. The release includes one zero-day and over 60 critical-rated vulnerabilities .

The total falls below October’s Patch Tuesday (1,413 flaws) but still makes this the second-largest monthly release on record. The release includes one zero-day and over 60 critical-rated vulnerabilities .

findings.summary: Hackers exploiting AhsayCBS backup servers have planted webshells, hidden encrypted code inside PNG images, and staged a Python implant designed to run only on its intended host. The findings show an intrusion that extended beyond cryptocurrency mining, giving attackers several ways to keep access to systems responsible for protecting an organization’s backups.

findings.summary: Microsoft researchers have demonstrated how small changes to an AI model can implant a hidden backdoor, causing an agent to execute an attacker’s command when a specific trigger appears. The technique, called Lazarus, requires no model retraining and allows the agent to behave normally during standard safety evaluations.

findings.summary: Microsoft has released security updates for four Windows Remote Desktop Client vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to run code through network connections or local access. Published on November 10, 2026, the flaws involve memory handling errors and a timing issue. Three have network attack paths, while the fourth requires an attacker with existing local access, an important difference when assessing exposure.

findings.summary: The Git project patched six vulnerabilities, including a critical flaw that allows malicious repositories to execute code during recursive cloning. The other five involve unsafe file writes and memory corruption in merges and patches. Git announced the fixes on November 10, 2026. The patches arrive in Git 2.56.1. They are also backported to 2.55.1, 2.54.1, 2.53.1, 2.52.1, 2.51.3, and 2.50.2. Users should move to 2.56.1 or the latest fix for their release line.

findings.summary: Microsoft has disclosed two Windows BitLocker security feature bypass vulnerabilities that could allow attackers with physical access to weaken device protections. Published on November 10, 2026, the flaws are tracked as CVE-2026-97015 and CVE-2026-119832. Microsoft rates both as Important, with CVSS base scores of 6.8 and 5.9, respectively. The bugs have different causes and access requirements, so security teams should assess each separately.

findings.summary: Google has patched CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity use-after-free in Chrome’s XML handling that attackers are already exploiting. The fix landed in the Stable channel on November 9, 2026, three days after an anonymous researcher reported the bug. Google says it is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild. It is the eighth exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 10. What Is CVE-2026-125350?

findings.summary: Claude Code helped uncover a technique that can turn an otherwise capable AI model into a sleeper agent by changing fewer than 10 dormant neurons. Called Lazarus, the method plants a hidden backdoor in model weights, allowing an attacker’s trigger to make an AI agent produce commands that download and run malicious code. The model can still pass standard evaluations and behave normally during routine tasks.
findings.title: Claude Code AI Discovers Technique to Turn Dormant Model Neurons Into Hidden Malware Triggers

findings.summary: A public exploit called SignDrop targets a Windows security feature meant to stop attacks on the Common Log File System (CLFS). It claims to turn a normal user account into a SYSTEM account, the highest level of control on Windows. The flaw has no CVE number and no patch as of November 11, 2026. Microsoft has also not confirmed the claims.
findings.title: Windows SignDrop 0-Day Exploit Lets Attackers Gain SYSTEM Privileges Through CLFS Protection

findings.summary: Security analysts already ask AI assistants to summarize CVEs, draft reports and explain unfamiliar techniques. Ask the same assistant which of your domains were impersonated this week, and it can only guess: it has no view of your alarms, your assets or your executives’ leaked credentials. The SOCRadar MCP Server closes that gap.
findings.title: SOCRadar MCP: 126 Tools and the New MSSP MCP Server

findings.summary: In this article From scans to reports Selected findings Closing thoughts At Microsoft’s FORGE Lab , we used codename MDASH to scan a subset of Linux kernel subsystems from late May to mid-June 2026. One full-time researcher and one intern led this three-month effort, which has so far produced 59 public upstream reports and 33 assigned CVEs . We confirmed working root privilege-escalation exploits for eight of those CVEs, and fixes for 38 of our reports have been merged into mainline.
findings.title: Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports

findings.summary: The Node.js project has released fixes for 16 security flaws across its 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines. Seven are rated high, six medium, and three low. findings.summary: Apache has fixed a critical bug in its HTTP/2 module that could let a remote attacker run code on a web server. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-119618 and affects mod_http2. The fix came on November 11, 2026, in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71. The bug sits in a function called assign_headers(). Apache says it is a concurrency problem, where shared resources are used without proper locking. Put simply, two parts of the code can touch the same piece of memory at the same time.

findings.summary: A new ransomware group called Citrus is using Windows Group Policy to push its malware across entire company networks and switch off Microsoft Defender first. Group Policy is a trusted Windows tool that admins use to manage many computers at once. Here, the attackers turn it into a delivery system. The group breaks in through stolen contractor logins, then moves slowly through the network until it controls a domain controller. From there, one policy change can reach every connected machine.

findings.summary: Microsoft’s FORGE Lab used an AI-driven scanning system to find 59 security bugs in the Linux kernel. Some of them sat unnoticed for more than 20 years. The work has so far led to 33 assigned CVEs, and Microsoft confirmed working root privilege-escalation exploits for eight of them. The team used a tool with the codename MDASH. It scanned selected kernel areas from late May to mid-June 2026, and a full-time researcher and an intern led the three-month effort.

findings.summary: Microsoft has warned that attackers are using a free remote access tool called GSocket to stay inside Linux servers even after the original security hole is fixed. Many admins treat a patch as the end of an incident, but this activity shows that patching alone may leave the attacker’s access untouched. GSocket is an open source tool built for remote administration. Attackers have turned it into a quiet backdoor because it hides its traffic inside a shared public relay network.

findings.summary: Users trust a cloud provider to configure and maintain their IT services, including data storage. In turn, the provider guarantees that hosted services will stay up and that data will remain strictly confidential. To demonstrate that their platforms are secure, providers choose different strategies: some run bug bounty programs, some rely on regular internal audits, and some bring in external research teams.

findings.summary: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token.

findings.summary: On 12 November 2026, the Cloud Software Group published security bulletins for its Citrix products addressing 28 memory flaws in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway. One of these vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-120868, affects every deployment, including those using the default configuration. The vendor bulletin describes the impact as unpredictable behaviour and denial of service. Citrix reports no exploitation, and no public proof-of-concept has been confirmed.

findings.summary: A vulnerability in the Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser of Cisco BroadWorks could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system. This vulnerability exists because XML entries are improperly parsed due to external entity resolution being allowed by default. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted XML message to the Open Client Interface – Provisioning (OCI-P) service.
findings.title: Cisco BroadWorks Out-of-Band Blind XML External Entity Injection Vulnerability

findings.summary: ### Impact An unauthenticated caller able to reach the query endpoint could exhaust database and server resources with ordinary, inexpensive requests. The keyword-search arm read the entire corpus on every request and rebuilt an in-memory BM25 index from it, so the cost of serving a query scaled with the size of the source table rather than with the size of the result set.
findings.title: pgEdge RAG Server unbounded corpus read allows resource exhaustion from unauthenticated requests

findings.summary: ### Summary Every `pg_hba.conf` generated by the pgEdge Control Plane begins with a hard-coded block of `trust` entries covering Unix-socket and loopback connections. Any operating-system account that can reach the Postgres socket or the loopback interface on a database host can authenticate as any Postgres role, including the superuser, without presenting a credential.
findings.title: pgEdge Control Plane generates pg_hba.conf with trust authentication for local and loopback connections

findings.summary: ### Impact `ActionController::Parameters#each_key` delegates to the internal `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess` that holds the request parameters, so when called with a block it returns that hash instead of the `Parameters` instance. The hash does not respond to `permitted?`, so Active Model mass assignment (`new`, `assign_attributes`, `update`) accepts it without raising `ActiveModel::ForbiddenAttributesError`.
findings.title: Action Pack: Possible Strong Parameters Bypass in Parameters#each_key

findings.summary: ## Summary Matching a selector that uses the descendant combinator (`a b`) takes time that grows polynomially with how deeply the document is nested, and each extra descendant combinator in the selector raises the degree by one. A selector with `k` descendant combinators takes `O(n^(k+1))` time on a chain of `n` nested elements.
findings.title: Soup Sieve: Polynomial-time denial of service in the descendant combinator

findings.summary: Beast ransomware has a hidden control panel. findings.summary: A new espionage group is using Windows named pipes and the SMB file-sharing protocol to move malware through tightly separated networks. Positive Technologies calls the group StingyBasilisk. It has been active since at least April 2022. The attackers sat quietly inside the victim’s systems for a long time and posed as the organization’s own security tools. The team could not find out how the attackers first got in.

findings.summary: 4EverAble2Shell is an N-central zero-day exploit chain that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run commands as root on an on-premises N-able N-central server. An independent researcher released a proof of concept (PoC) early on November 12, 2026, and attackers used it to install cryptocurrency miners on at least 21 servers within hours. The chain works against fully patched servers when the Legacy API is turned on and reachable from the internet.

findings.summary: The Apache Software Foundation has released Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 to fix CVE-2026-119618 , a critical race condition in the mod_http2 module that can lead to Remote Code Execution (RCE) . Any server running httpd 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 with HTTP/2 enabled is in scope, and the attacker needs no credentials or user interaction. No active exploitation attempts or compromises have been observed to date.
findings.title: CVE-2026-119618: Apache HTTP/2 Race Condition RCE

findings.summary: Hackers are sending fake purchase order emails to trick recipients into opening Word documents that deliver XLoader, an information-stealing malware. The attack uses an embedded document, an old Microsoft Equation Editor vulnerability, and several script stages to reach its final payload. What begins as a routine order confirmation can end with stolen browser data and additional malware on an infected computer.
findings.title: Hackers Use Fake Purchase Order Emails to Deliver XLoader Malware Through Malicious Word Documents

findings.summary: Citrix has released fixes for 28 security flaws in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. One of them, CVE-2026-120868, affects every deployment in its default setup. Cloud Software Group published bulletin CTX697305 on November 12, 2026, and rated it Critical. CVE-2026-120868 is a memory overflow in packet processing . It carries a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.3. Most NetScaler bugs need a specific feature turned on. This one does not.

findings.summary: A new campaign is guessing its way into internet-facing Microsoft SQL Server systems. The attackers use a list of more than 2,700 passwords and then install a cryptocurrency miner and a remote access trojan (RAT) on the hacked machines. The campaign has been running since at least early October 2026. Database servers hold valuable data, so they are a favorite target. This campaign scans for exposed servers, tries many logins, and runs commands that pull in more malware.
findings.title: Hackers Use 2,700 Passwords to Break Into Microsoft SQL Servers and Deploy Remote Access Malware

findings.summary: Three Trezor Safe 5 wallets bought from the reseller CryptoBilis contain an implant, an extra circuit board that can copy their recovery phrases, hardware wallet maker Trezor said yesterday. The implant reads the phrase from the wallet's screen and sends it over the mobile network to a server controlled by the attackers. The company examined one of the wallets in its lab, identified the other
findings.title: Trezor Confirms Hidden Implants in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallets That Can Steal Recovery Phrases

findings.summary: Hackers are hiding cryptocurrency mining on Linux GPU servers by changing the readings administrators use to spot heavy workloads. The toolkit combines a Rust-based controller called SANSAR, a kernel rootkit, and a modified NVIDIA monitoring library that reports 0% GPU utilization while mining continues in the background. The intrusion reached three Linux GPU hosts through an exposed Ray job agent.
findings.title: Hackers Use SANSAR Linux Malware to Hide Crypto Mining by Faking 0% GPU Usage

findings.summary: A simple typing mistake can now cost you more than a failed page load. Researchers have found that mistyped addresses of popular AI tools lead to fake verification pages, hidden commands and malware installers. The technique is called TypoPrompting. findings.summary: ## Summary The public CCG lexicon parser `nltk.ccg.lexicon.fromstring` parses caller-influenced lexicon text with two pure-Python loops whose cost is quadratic in the input width. A service that parses an untrusted CCG lexicon string can be driven into tens of seconds of single-threaded CPU by a few-megabyte input, starving the request worker. No authentication or user interaction is required.
findings.title: NLTK: Quadratic-time CPU denial of service in CCG lexicon parser (fromstring) on wide bracket bodies and operator chains

findings.summary: ## Summary `Tree.chomsky_normal_form()` binarizes a parse tree and defaults to right factoring. For a node with N children the right-factor branch repeatedly removes the first element of a working list with `list.pop(0)`, which shifts all remaining elements each time, so binarizing one wide node costs O(N^2). An application that converts an attacker-supplied treebank tree to Chomsky Normal Form can be forced into tens of seconds of single-threaded CPU by one wide flat tree.
findings.title: NLTK: Quadratic-time CPU denial of service in Tree.chomsky_normal_form right-factor binarization via list.pop(0)
